about.title: Hollister Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary day in Hollister into a trip to the emergency room — whether it's a malfunctioning tool on a San Benito County farm, a faulty appliance in a home near San Felipe Road, or a vehicle part failure along Rt 25. Unlike many injury cases, California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm — not on proving someone was careless. That distinction matters, and it's one reason people reach out after a product-related injury. Our team evaluates what happened, helps preserve the product as evidence, and explains whether the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may share responsibility. The initial review costs nothing, and we only get paid if there's a recovery. If a product hurt you or someone you love in Hollister, it's worth finding out where you stand.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California often applies strict liability to defective products, meaning the injured person generally must show the product was flawed and caused harm — not that the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the pool of parties we can pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: We can advise you on keeping the product itself intact and unaltered, since it often serves as the central piece of evidence in these claims.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try not to alter, repair, or throw it away, even if it's damaged. The product itself is usually the most important evidence in a defect claim, and we can advise you on how to store or document it properly.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, so the focus is typically on whether the product was defective and caused your injury rather than on proving negligence.

items.question: Are product liability injuries common in Hollister?
items.answer: Hollister sees a range of injury incidents each year, including some tied to defective products used at home, on the job, or on corridors like San Felipe Road and 4th Street. We can review the specifics of your situation and explain your options.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free initial case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
